title: Continuous precomposition of injective modules has trivial positive Cech cohomology
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites, with objects, arrows, covering indices and coefficient values in one common universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be continuous in the covering-family sense [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](3): it sends coverings to coverings and preserves their pullbacks along any map. Let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal D$ and $I$ an injective sheaf of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Then $R_u(V)=R(uV)$ and $I_u(V)=I(uV)$, with restrictions $R(u(h))$ and $I(u(h))$ and scalar action inherited sectionwise, are a ring sheaf and an $R_u$-module sheaf on $\mathcal C$. Write $I_{\mathrm{ab}}$ and $(I_u)_{\mathrm{ab}}$ for their underlying abelian sheaves.
For every covering $\mathcal U=\{U_t\to U\}_{t\in T}$, use the chosen iterated fibre products and alternating Cech complexes of [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex]. For $n\geq0$ and $\mathbf t\in T^{n+1}$ put $W_{\mathbf t}=U_{t_0}\times_U\cdots\times_UU_{t_n}$ and $P_{\mathbf t}=uU_{t_0}\times_{uU}\cdots\times_{uU}uU_{t_n}$. The canonical maps $c_{\mathbf t}:uW_{\mathbf t}\to P_{\mathbf t}$ are isomorphisms and satisfy
$$c_{\mathbf t\setminus t_j}\circ u(\delta_j)=\delta_j\circ c_{\mathbf t}$$
for the projections deleting a factor. In $D^+(\operatorname{Ab})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] there is a canonical isomorphism
$$Q\check C^\bullet(\mathcal U,(I_u)_{\mathrm{ab}})\xrightarrow{\sim}Q\check C^\bullet(u\mathcal U,I_{\mathrm{ab}}),$$
where $Q$ is localization at quasi-isomorphisms. It is represented by the cochain isomorphism whose component at $\mathbf t$ is $I(c_{\mathbf t}^{-1}):I(uW_{\mathbf t})\to I(P_{\mathbf t})$. In particular $\check H^q(\mathcal U,(I_u)_{\mathrm{ab}})=0$ for every $q>0$. No cocontinuity, preservation of arbitrary fibre products, or injectivity of $I_{\mathrm{ab}}$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0D6X, lemma-pullback-injective-pre-limp, proof: covering-nerve comparison and injective-module Cech vanishing before applying lemma-cech-vanish-collection.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-site-continuous-pushforward-sheaf], precomposition sends the underlying set sheaf of $R$ and the abelian sheaf $I_{\mathrm{ab}}$ to sheaves. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-sheaf-iff-underlying-sets] to the ring presheaf $V\mapsto R(uV)$ to obtain the ring sheaf $R_u$. Define its action on $I_u(V)$ by the given $R(uV)$-action. The module laws hold sectionwise, and for $h:V\to W$ one has $I(u(h))(as)=R(u(h))(a)I(u(h))(s)$. Thus [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] gives exactly the asserted $R_u$-module sheaf, with the stated restrictions.

Fix $\mathcal U$. Continuity sends it to a covering and supplies the canonical pullback isomorphism for every $U_t\to U$ and every $V\to U$. These are precisely the hypotheses of [lem-trf-continuous-cover-nerve-comparison]. Its conclusion gives the projection-characterized isomorphisms $c_{\mathbf t}$ for all positive tuple lengths, and its index-map equation for the increasing injection omitting $j$ is $c_{\mathbf t\setminus t_j}u(\delta_{W,j})=\delta_{P,j}c_{\mathbf t}$. This proves both geometric clauses for the choices in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0D6X (lemma-pullback-injective-pre-limp), proof, displayed iterated fibre-product identity; Sites Tag 00WV.

proof.text: Put $K=\check C^\bullet(\mathcal U,(I_u)_{\mathrm{ab}})$ and $L=\check C^\bullet(u\mathcal U,I_{\mathrm{ab}})$. Define $A^n(s)_{\mathbf t}=I(c_{\mathbf t}^{-1})(s_{\mathbf t})$ for $n\ge0$ and use the unique map between zero groups for $n<0$. Its inverse in each degree is $B^n(r)_{\mathbf t}=I(c_{\mathbf t})(r_{\mathbf t})$, since restrictions respect identities and composition. For $\mathbf r=\mathbf t\setminus t_j$, step 2 gives $u(\delta_{W,j})c_{\mathbf t}^{-1}=c_{\mathbf r}^{-1}\delta_{P,j}$, hence contravariance gives $I(c_{\mathbf t}^{-1})I(u(\delta_{W,j}))=I(\delta_{P,j})I(c_{\mathbf r}^{-1})$. Sum this identity with signs $(-1)^j$. The differential formula of [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex] yields $A^{n+1}d_K^n=d_L^nA^n$; it is automatic in negative degrees. Multiplying by $B^{n+1}$ and $B^n$ gives $d_K^nB^n=B^{n+1}d_L^n$. Thus $A$ and $B$ are inverse cochain maps with the required component formula.

source.place: Tag 0D6X, proof, Cech comparison, expanded using Tag 03AM (definition-cech-complex), equation-d-cech.

proof.text: Both complexes vanish in negative degrees by [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex]. Applying the localization functor $Q$ of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] to $AB=1$ and $BA=1$ gives inverse morphisms in $D^+(\operatorname{Ab})$. This is the stated isomorphism represented by $A$. It is canonical: the maps $c_{\mathbf t}$ are uniquely characterized by their projections, so the component formula determines $A$ without any additional choices beyond the chosen fibre products.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-injective-module-cech-acyclic] to the ringed site $(\mathcal D,R)$, its injective $R$-module $I$, and the covering $u\mathcal U$. Its common-universe size restriction agrees with ours, and the site axioms are those assumed here; the small-site sheafification is the usual one. Its conclusion is $H^q(L)=0$ for $q>0$, without assuming $I_{\mathrm{ab}}$ injective. The inverse cochain maps of step 3 restrict to inverse maps on kernels and images and therefore induce inverse maps on the quotients defining cohomology in [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex]. Consequently $\check H^q(\mathcal U,(I_u)_{\mathrm{ab}})=H^q(K)=0$ for $q>0$.
